body: @mkouba do you have an idea about this ?

> @mkouba do you have an idea about this ?

No idea so far. I need to take a good look at the reproducer. In any case, the `@ActivateRequestContext` should not be needed for async observers because the request context is always active during notification.

It seems that a new request context is not activated during the notification because the thread that is used has an associated Vertx _duplicated context_ with the request context state from the thread that was used to handle the `org.acme.Resource.execute()` resource method... which is really weird :thinking: CC @cescoffier 

Note that we use the `ExecutorService` obtained from the `ExecutorBuildItem` (i.e. the  executor for blocking tasks) for notification of async observers. 

What's also weird is that if I stop the execution during debugging in the `EventImpl.Notifier.notify()` method before the observer is notified and wait a little then a new context is not activated but the test passes.

It turns out that the [Vertx context is captured](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/2.14.0.Final/extensions/vertx/runtime/src/main/java/io/quarkus/vertx/core/runtime/VertxCoreRecorder.java#L549-L573) when a new task is submitted from a thread of the default blocking `ExecutorService` and restored when the task is executed on a different thread. I would not expect this kind of behavior but it's implemented this way for a long time (probably because of some Mutiny use cases?). As a result, the https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/pull/27443 caused this regression.

> I would not expect this kind of behavior but it's implemented this way for a long time

Note that the capture/restore makes it possible to access the vertx context concurrently from multiple threads.

issue.title: When propagating the duplicated context, drop the request scope
